newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa tells CNMV won't sell Viesgo, Nansa.
newsitem.headline: Endesa tells CNMV won't sell Viesgo, Nansa.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Endesa told stock market watchdog CNMV late on Tuesday it was not prepared to sell its stakes in Electra de Viesgo and Saltos de Nansa.
"There is no intention of accepting any buy offer from a third party," it said in a note.
Press reports on Monday said Hidrocantabrico was interested in buying Endesa's stakes in the two smaller firms, prompting the CNMV to suspend trading in all three.
In a separate note to the CNMV, Hidrocantabrico said it had conducted a preliminary analysis of a possible purchase of the stakes but confirmed there had been no talks with Endesa.
"Hidroelectrica del Cantabrico has not adopted any decision to present a buy offer for the stakes," it said.
Endesa added that Union Fenosa did not form part of the operational group formed by the Grupo Endesa companies.

"If the current indirect stake (in Fenosa) was considered inconvenient in the framework of the current reorganisation of the electrical sector, Endesa would proceed to sell the aforementioned stake," it said.
Endesa, which is 66-percent state-owned, must divest holdings in groups such as Union Fenosa, Viesgo and Nansa under a plan announced on Friday to buy up to 75 percent of Sevillana and Fecsa.
